title: Teaching Assistant Professor of Business Law - General Business - Chambers College
description:
The Department of General Business in the John Chambers College of
Business and Economics at West Virginia University (located in
Morgantown, WV) invites applications for a Teaching Assistant
Professor – Business Law. This position is expected to begin in
January 2027. The position will involve teaching under the
Department of General Business, with a research and service
affiliation to the Knee Regulatory Research Center (KRRC), focusing
on topics related to business law, regulation, and healthcare
policy.

The primary teaching responsibility for this position is business
law, with courses drawn from the candidate's area of expertise.
Candidates should demonstrate a teaching philosophy that emphasizes
experiential learning and student engagement. The successful
candidate will potentially be to teaching at the undergraduate
and/or graduate levels as the needs of the department dictate.
Teaching is intended to be primarily focused within the Online MBA
Program of the College. Candidates are also expected to collaborate
with colleagues to support and strengthen the college's innovative,
student-centered culture during this period of rapid program
growth.

While the position is primarily teaching-focused, the candidate
will be expected to bring practical experience with how regulations
and policy work together, and knowledge of how policy is changed
through legislation at the state and federal level, into the
classroom.

The successful candidate will have the opportunity to collaborate
with scholars within the Knee Regulatory Research Center, under the
direction of Dr. Alicia Plemmons, Director of KRRC. Candidates with
a J.D. or Ph.D. in law, business, public policy, or a related field
with experience in regulatory or legislative analysis are
encouraged to apply. Salary and benefits will be competitive and
commensurate with experience and qualifications. The position and
start date are subject to budget approval.

Qualifications :

Qualified candidates must hold, at the time of appointment, a J.D.
or Ph.D. in law, business, public policy, or a related field, with
demonstrated experience in regulatory and legislative processes at
the state and/or federal level. Candidates in the advanced stages
of a J.D. or Ph.D. will also be considered but must have completed
their degree before the start date of this position.

West Virginia University (and the John Chambers College of Business
and Economics) is particularly interested in candidates who can
contribute, through their teaching and service, to the excellence
of the academic community.

Application Process

Review of applications will begin immediately and will continue
until the position is filled. Applicants must submit the following
items electronically: (1) a letter of interest, (2) curriculum
vitae, (3) a statement of teaching philosophy, (4) a writing
sample, and (5) contact information for three references.

Please submit applications electronically at https://careers.wvu.edu/career-opportunities
.

General inquiries may be directed to Dr. Alicia Plemmons, Director
of the Knee Regulatory Research Center and Associate Professor of
General Business, at Alicia.Plemmons@mail.wvu.edu
.
